description: I’m a third-year Computer Science student passionate about AI/ML, Python, data science, and building innovative solutions to real-world problems. I’m looking for enthusiastic teammates with skills in AI/ML, web development, data analysis, UI/UX, and creative problem-solving who are excited to collaborate and build something impactful for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026!
summary:
SpaceVerse is an interactive 3‑D web application that lets users explore a virtual solar system and conduct scientific missions on planets, moons, and spacecraft. Built with Vite, React, and Three.js, the app provides a realistic physics‑based environment where users can launch rockets, operate orbital labs, and manage resources such as fuel and power. The codebase includes a rich component library (e.g., LunarFlybyLab, RocketAssemblyStage, SpaceCampaignMap) alongside data modules that define celestial bodies and mission parameters.

The challenge addressed by SpaceVerse is to make complex space‑flight concepts accessible through an engaging, browser‑based experience without requiring heavyweight desktop software or specialized hardware. By bundling the simulation logic, visual assets, and UI into a single, easily deployable project, the app enables educators, hobbyists, and developers to demonstrate orbital mechanics, mission planning, and spacecraft design in real time. Its open‑source nature encourages community contributions, fostering a collaborative platform for learning and prototyping future space‑technology ideas.
details:
SpaceVerse // GALAXY-X
Interactive 3D Aerospace Mission Campus & Flight Simulation Platform

  1. What Does It Do or How Does It Work?

SpaceVerse is a browser-based, interactive 3D aerospace mission campus and flight simulation platform. Rather than presenting static quiz cards or flat menus, SpaceVerse places the user in the boots of an aerospace engineer and flight director inside a live NASA Space Center Campus built with Three.js and React.

How It Works:

  1. Interactive 3D Campus Navigation: Players navigate in real-time across six specialized aerospace campus sectors:
  • SAH (Spacecraft Assembly Hangar): Cleanroom bays for satellite staging and mechanical integration.
  • LCC (Launch Control Complex & Pad 39X): Multi-stage launch vehicle assembly, pad staging, and countdown sequencing.
  • GSC (Ground Station & Deep Space Network): Antenna array telemetry tracking, orbit power monitoring, and interplanetary signal downlink.
  • MPR (Mission Planning Room): Trajectory calculation holo-tables and environmental stress testing.
  • PNL (Propulsion & Navigation Lab): Fuel-mass ratio calibration and orbital delta-V calculations.
  • MCC (Mission Control Center): Real-time orbital monitoring, telemetry consoles, and emergency response.
  1. Eight Scaffolding Mission Levels:
  • Level 1 - Satellite Assembly (SAH): Snap-fitting 9 essential subsystems (Bus frame, Solar wings, Battery pack, S-Band antenna, Multispectral camera, Propulsion thrusters, On-Board Computer, ADCS reaction wheels, Thermal radiator louvers) with live validation of mass, power, and telemetry tags.
  • Level 2 - Rocket Assembly & Launch (LCC & Pad 39X): 10-module multi-stage rocket construction (boosters, cryogenic tanks, interstage, avionics, payload fairing), pad staging, ignition sequence, aerodynamic ascent, and orbital insertion.
  • Level 3 - Orbit & Power Management (GSC): Balancing solar panel power generation against battery capacity to ensure spacecraft survival through the dark eclipse of Earth's shadow.
  • Level 4 - Environmental Shake & Freeze Test (MPR): Acoustic/vibration qualification on a shaker table (70 pts or higher target) and thermal vacuum cryogenic chamber testing (-20°C survivability) within strict mass limits (500 kg or less).
  • Level 5 - Lunar Flyby Fuel Math (PNL): Calculating the optimal propellant balance (45-65 kg) to generate sufficient delta-V for a 238,000-mile lunar transfer without exceeding rocket payload lift limits.
  • Level 6 - Thermometer Telemetry Probe (Europa Discovery): Deep-space mission over 628 million km to Jupiter's icy moon Europa; landing on a procedural 3D ice basin, calibrating sensors, drilling into cryo-fissures, and downlinking thermal readings to Earth.
  • Level 7 - Lunar Water Hunt (Moon South Pole Expedition): Exploring permanently shadowed craters (Cabeus, Shackleton, Faustini) using neutron spectrometers and ice-penetrating radar to confirm subsurface water ice.
  • Level 8 - Astronaut EVA Rescue (ISS Low Earth Orbit): Emergency spacewalk rescue 408 km above Earth. Radar-locking a drifting astronaut, dodging space debris, matching orbital velocity, and deploying the robotic arm for capture.
  1. In-Game Engineering Handbook & Dialogue:
  • Flight Director Vance: Features a voice-briefed mission commander avatar providing spoken situational updates and mission context.
  • Spacecraft Engineering Handbook: An illustrated technical guide explaining aerospace principles through intuitive analogies, troubleshooting cheatsheets, and concept mastery quizzes.
  1. What Benefits Does It Have?
  • Hands-on STEM Experiential Learning: Replaces abstract textbook formulas with interactive cause-and-effect simulations (for example, if you undersize your battery pack, your satellite de-powers during eclipse; if you overload fuel, the rocket fails to lift off).
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Operates entirely in modern web browsers via WebGL—no high-end flight sim rigs, expensive software licenses, or gigabyte-heavy installations required.
  • Systems-Thinking Mastery: Teaches players how aerospace disciplines interconnect: mechanical structures, electrical power, thermodynamics, orbital mechanics, communication link budgets, and cost/weight optimization.
  • Immediate Telemetry & Failure Scaffolding: Provides real-time feedback with explicit diagnostic notes explaining why an assembly failed or why an orbit decayed, fostering scientific inquiry and resilience.
  1. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?
  • Democratizing Aerospace Education: Giving K-12 students, university engineering recruits, and space enthusiasts worldwide equal access to high-fidelity space mission design tools.
  • Inspiring the Artemis Generation: Cultivating interest in lunar exploration, deep-space planetary science (Europa Clipper), and orbital space safety (debris mitigation and astronaut rescue).
  • Bridging Theory and Practice: Demonstrating how physics, mathematics, and computer science apply directly to real missions conducted by NASA, ESA, and commercial spaceflight organizations.
  1. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Were Used?
  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (ESNext), HTML5, CSS3, GLSL shader techniques
  • 3D Engine & Graphics: Three.js (WebGL renderer, RoomEnvironment PBR lighting, custom procedural geometry, camera controls, Raycasting)
  • UI & Animation: React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Motion (Framer Motion), Lucide React icons, custom SVG technical diagrams
  • Audio Engine: Custom Web Audio API procedural synthesizer (real-time sound synthesis for rocket roar, ignition rumble, radio static, and telemetry beeps)
  • Build & Tooling: Vite, tsx, Node.js
  • Backend & APIs: Node.js Express, RESTful endpoints, local persistence registry
  • Database & Cloud: Google Firebase Authentication & Google Cloud Firestore with local JSON fallback (galaxyx-db.json)
  • AI Capabilities: Configured with Google Gemini API (@google/genai) for dynamic mission intelligence
  • Target Hardware: Runs cross-platform on standard consumer laptops, desktops, and Chromebooks with WebGL-capable GPUs
  1. How Is Your Project Creative?
  • The 3D Campus Metaphor: Instead of traditional menu dropdowns, users interact with a physical 3D space center campus featuring sector signage, walking navigation, and proximity-activated workstations.
    • Chassis/Bus = Skeleton
    • On-Board Computer = Brain
    • Solar Panels & Batteries = Heart & Metabolism
    • Multispectral Sensors = Eyes
    • High-Gain Antenna = Voice
  • Procedural Planetary Surface Explorers: Custom 3D heightmapped terrain renderers for both the Moon's South Pole and Europa's fractured icy crust.
  1. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?
  2. Scientific Fidelity vs. User Accessibility:
  • Consideration: Real orbital mechanics and thermal calculations involve advanced differential equations that could intimidate beginners.
  • Solution: We preserved the real physics (mass trade-offs, cryogenic temperatures in Celsius/Kelvin, solar flux vs. battery watt-hours, delta-V limits) while encapsulating them into intuitive visual sliders, gauges, and instant telemetry cards.
  1. Web Performance & Load Times:
  • Consideration: Heavy 3D assets often cause long loading screens and lag on classroom computers or mobile devices.
  • Solution: Built lightweight procedural 3D meshes and procedural textures directly in Three.js code, keeping the initial bundle fast, responsive, and lightweight.
  1. Resilience & Offline-First Architecture:
  • Consideration: Unstable internet connections in classrooms or remote environments shouldn't interrupt learning.
  • Solution: Implemented dual data storage: seamless cloud synchronization via Firebase/Firestore when connected, paired with an automatic offline local JSON database fallback.
  1. Multimodal Learning (Audio, Visual, Kinesthetic):
  • Consideration: Different learners absorb information differently.
  • Solution: Integrated audio cues (Director Vance voice briefings, sound effects), visual diagrams (SVG schematics, 3D orbits), and interactive kinesthetic labs (dragging modules, snapping parts, dialing fuel values).
  1. Progressive Cognitive Scaffolding:
  • Consideration: Space exploration is vast and complex.
  • Solution: Structured the campaign into 8 clear stages, gradually ramping from elementary modular assembly to orbital mechanics, deep-space planetary science, and emergency spacecraft control.
